signals.verdict: TESTED 2026-08-05 against a hashed pre-registration, then RE-RUN THE SAME DAY on a CORRECTED primary outcome (sigtest/prereg_amendment.json A1: the old outcome carried the entry half of the toll inside its denominator) — FAILED both times, 0 survivors both times. Not wired into any gate, sizing or selection path. Recorded so it accumulates toward n>=300.
signals.outcome_definition: exit_price / px_in - 1 — a TRUE gross price move. The earlier definition (exit_price / entry - 1) had the entry-side toll inside its denominator and was then compared against a full round-trip toll, double-charging the entry push by ~2.2pp at the median.

underpowered_excluded_from_best.why: n=23 is below the pre-registered minimum of 30; it could not have survived at any p, so its favoured-half move is not the family best

exploratory_killed.label: hours to first reach $25k depth
exploratory_killed.status: KILLED — exploratory, 1 hit in 46 trials, failed OOS and every strip test
exploratory_killed.note: On the CORRECTED outcome it no longer clears BH either (p_bh 0.0966). And its sign is POSITIVE — more hours to reach $25k predicts a BETTER outcome — the OPPOSITE of the direction H1/H2 pre-register from Marino et al. Even had it been registered it would have failed S3 (sign) regardless of p. It is not a discarded Marino effect; it points the other way.

censoring_bound.bound: THIS TABLE CAN ONLY EVER RANK WALLETS THAT SELL OUT FAST. A position closes when the copied wallet exits, and exit speed is the exact variable the cited literature (Marino/Naviglio/Tarantelli/Lillo) names as the mechanism, so the sample is conditioned on the treatment. Any future 'who to copy' work needs an exit rule that closes on OUR OWN criteria — a time or price stop — or this selection never goes away, no matter how long the book runs.

persistence.question: are some wallets persistently worth copying?
persistence.verdict: NOT ANSWERABLE on the pre-registered gate (0 of 16 cells qualify), and the parts that ARE answerable say no
persistence.action_taken: NOTHING WIRED IN. No wallet gate, no wallet ranking, no re-weighting.
persistence.the_transfer_finding_that_survives: on the SAME 39 round trips the tracked wallet is up 74.4% of the time and we are up 17.9%; the difference decomposes into a round-trip toll they never pay.
persistence.what_was_WITHDRAWN_2026_08_05: ⚠️ 'their own median gross move +3.449346% vs our copy's +3.449326%, so we are NOT late and we DO capture their move' is a TAUTOLOGY and is withdrawn. The engine fills at the copied wallet's OWN observed price (px_raw = usd/amt) and exits at their own sell price, so the two moves are the same two prices by construction. There is no latency term in honest.py and the latency-decay measurement has never run: OUR SLIPPAGE FROM OUR OWN DETECTION DELAY IS UNMEASURED. Until it is measured, no claim of the form 'the picks are fine, only the cost is broken' may justify execution spend — a cheaper venue, a router or a faster box.

by_wallet.note: Per-wallet attribution, descriptive. Realised and unrealised are never on the same line. `clears_toll_gate` is the VERDICT form: the wallet's own median gross move against 2x its own median toll, computed BOTH on closed positions and on every position it triggered marked like this book's own headline, and FALSE whenever those two disagree. It is REPORTED, never enforced. It is None below 10 closes — a median on one trade is not a measurement, and the raw sub-threshold flag is published separately as `clears_toll_gate_unjudged_n`. Every interval on the row resamples TOKEN BLOCKS, so same-token re-entries minutes apart count as one bet, not several.
